title: Cyclic quintic covers of the line, x^5 = f(y,z)
summary: The plane quintics x^5 + f(y,z) form Moonen's special family of mu_5-covers of P^1 branched at 5 points; at p = 7 every member found is either mu-ordinary (codim 8) or supersingular, as the theory predicts.

metadata.family: mu_5-covers of P^1 with branch data a = (1,1,1,1,1), N = 5

provenance.note: First codim-8 find, x^5 + y^5 + z^5 + 2x^2y^3 (= z^5 + a binary quintic in x, y). Its polygon was absent from the Zenodo 18364679 data at p = 7.
Every island's codim-8 candidates and most supersingular curves had this form.
Supersingular curves from both runs classified up to F_7-isomorphism; mutator histories traced.

provenance.ref: B. Moonen, Special subvarieties arising from families of cyclic covers of the projective line, Doc. Math. 15 (2010), 793-819
provenance.note: The family satisfies Moonen's condition dim S = N - 3, so its image in A_6 is a special subvariety. The overseer knew of the family; the runs rediscovered it.

data: bead ne-3u14g: supersingular_p7.jsonl and classes.jsonl (not yet in the repository)
caveats: All polygons were computed with DeRham.jl 59b331b at table precision and are pending recomputation after the precision-bounds fix (bead ne-ez0l).
description: Let f(y,z) be a binary quintic with five distinct roots. The plane quintic C_f : x^5 = f(y,z) is smooth of genus 6, and x -> zeta_5 x makes it a cyclic degree-5 cover of P^1 branched at the five roots of f, each with local monodromy 1. As the branch points vary, these curves form a 2-dimensional family (5 points on P^1 up to PGL_2).
observations: At p = 7, counting distinct coefficient vectors separately in each FunSearch run: 50 curves of the form x^5 + f(y,z) have the codim-8 polygon 1/4^4 1/2^4 3/4^4, 16 are supersingular, and none has any other polygon. No curve outside the family reached codim 8.

The supersingular curves from both runs fall into 7 F_7-isomorphism classes, each merge backed by an explicit PGL_3(F_7) witness (bead ne-3u14g). Six lie in this family: x^5 + y^5 + z^5; x^5 + y^5 + z^5 + xy^4 + x^4y; x^5 + z^5 + y^2z^3 + 2y^3z^2 + y^4z; x^5 + y^5 + z^5 + y^2z^3 + 2y^3z^2; x^5 + y^4z + yz^4; x^5 + z^5 + 3y^3z^2 + y^4z. The seventh is the Klein-type quintic (entry 2).
The two dense supersingular curves from run 2 are Fermat in disguise: sums of fifth powers of three independent linear forms.
x^5 + y^4z + yz^4 is the case where f splits completely over F_7. All such curves are isomorphic over F_7, because PGL_2(F_7) is 3-transitive on P^1(F_7) and every element of F_7 is a fifth power.
explanation: Special family: on H^{1,0}, the eigenspaces for the characters j = 1, 2, 3, 4 have dimensions 3, 2, 1, 0, so the associated Shimura variety has dimension 3*0 + 2*1 = 2 = N - 3 (Moonen's condition).

Two polygons at p = 7: 7 has order 4 mod 5, so it is inert in Q(zeta_5). The isocrystal splits into four rank-3 pieces permuted cyclically by Frobenius, and the slopes are nu/4, with nu a slope of F^4 on one piece, each with multiplicity 4. Symmetry, the sum 6, the mu-ordinary bound (1,2,3) and integrality leave only nu = (1,2,3) (codim 8) and nu = (2,2,2) (supersingular).

Supersingular locus: by de Jong-Oort purity, the non-mu-ordinary locus has pure codimension 1 in the 2-dimensional family, so the supersingular locus is a curve, not isolated points. This is analogous to Picard modular surfaces at an inert prime.
Novelty: random sampling of all plane quintics, a 12-dimensional space, rarely lands in this 2-dimensional family, which is why the codim-8 polygon was missing from the Zenodo data.
open_questions: A complete survey at p = 7: finitely many F_7-classes of squarefree binary quintics f. It would confirm the two-polygon prediction and list every F_7-point of the supersingular curve.
Primes p = 1 mod 5 (11, 31, 41): the mu-ordinary polygon should be ordinary, with an intermediate stratum in codimension 1. Not yet checked.
Primes p = 4 mod 5 (19, 29): predicted mu-ordinary polygon 0^2 1/2^8 1^2 and again only two strata.
references: B. Moonen, Special subvarieties arising from families of cyclic covers of the projective line, Doc. Math. 15 (2010), 793-819.
A. J. de Jong and F. Oort, Purity of the stratification by Newton polygons, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 13 (2000), 209-241.

title: Klein-type quintic plus one monomial
summary: Adding one monomial to the Hurwitz-Klein quintic K = x^4y + y^4z + z^4x gives the codimension-9 polygon at p=7; at p=11, K is supersingular and one-term additions reach a codimension-3 polygon.

metadata.base_curve: K = x^4y + y^4z + z^4x (Hurwitz, Klein or Snyder quintic; H_{4,1})
metadata.family: K + t*m, m a monomial outside the support of K, t in F_p

provenance.note: FunSearch mutators explored additions to K and found K + x^3z^2, the first known plane quintic over F_7 with polygon 1/3^6 2/3^6. The mutator's reasoning predicted no polygon (bead ne-52i39).
All 18 single-monomial additions with coefficient 1 at p = 7.

provenance.ref: t-sweep 2026-10-29 by kurt (no bead; the bead store was down)
provenance.note: All 18 monomials with every t in F_7^*, 108 curves, same DeRham build and precision.
K itself is well studied; no published treatment of K + t*m or of the codim-9 polygon for this family was found.
First observed K alone with the supersingular polygon 1/2^12 at p=11.
The consistent evaluator saw 80 OK supersingular K samples. Program 104 scored S=2.5 and adds t*x^5 to K, giving the codimension-3 polygon.
The consistent evaluator saw 52 OK supersingular K samples. Programs 206, 228 and 229 each scored S=2.5 and add t*z^5 to K, giving the codimension-3 polygon.

caveats: All polygons were computed with DeRham.jl 59b331b at table precision and are pending recomputation after the precision-bounds fix (bead ne-ez0l).
description: K = x^4y + y^4z + z^4x is a smooth plane quintic of genus 6 and a quotient of the degree-13 Fermat curve. Its only coordinate-permutation symmetries are the rotations x -> y -> z -> x; a transposition reverses the orientation of the cycle. We study K + t*m for the 18 monomials m outside the support of K.
observations: K alone is supersingular at p = 7: slopes 1/2^12, codim 12, in both FunSearch runs and in the ne-76u21 recomputation. K with coefficients (1, 2, 3) on its three terms is the same F_7-isomorphism class (bead ne-3u14g), as expected: diagonal scaling normalizes the three coefficients.

Over the algebraic closure, K has the rotation x -> y -> z -> x and a diagonal mu_13. The mu_13 acts on K's three terms by a single character, and of the 21 quintic monomials only K's own three have that character. So adding any one monomial breaks every diagonal symmetry of K, and also the rotation. K + t*x^3z^2 keeps none of K's coordinate symmetries, yet it is codim 9 for t = 1, ..., 5 and supersingular at t = -1 over F_7. Other kinds of automorphism have not been ruled out.

With t = 1 the rotations split the 18 monomials into 6 orbits, each with a single polygon (all 18 computed): {x^3z^2, x^2y^3, y^2z^3}: 1/3^6 2/3^6, codim 9; {x^2z^3, x^3y^2, y^3z^2}: 0^2 1/3^3 1/2^2 2/3^3 1^2, codim 5; {x^5, y^5, z^5}: 0^3 1/2^6 1^3, codim 4; {xyz^3, x^3yz, xy^3z}: 0^4 1/2^4 1^4, codim 2; {yz^4, x^4z, xy^4}: 0^4 1/2^4 1^4, codim 2; {x^2yz^2, x^2y^2z, xy^2z^2}: ordinary.
The codim-9 polygon does not occur in the Zenodo 18364679 data at p = 7.

Varying t over F_7^* (all 18 monomials, 108 curves): every orbit keeps its t = 1 polygon at every smooth t. The exception is the codim-9 orbit: K + t*x^3z^2 has 1/3^6 2/3^6 for t = 1, ..., 5 and is supersingular at t = -1 (likewise for x^2y^3 and y^2z^3). Every other orbit has exactly one singular member in t in F_7^* (t = 3 for x^2z^3 and x^2yz^2, t = 2 for x^5 and yz^4, t = 6 for xyz^3); the codim-9 orbit has none.
So codim 9 is the generic behaviour of the pencil K + t*x^3z^2 over F_7, not an isolated fibre, and that pencil has two supersingular members, t = 0 (K) and t = -1.

Rescaling x, y, z cannot change t over F_7: the diagonal scalings that preserve K up to a constant (a^4b = b^4c = c^4a) fix the coefficient of x^3z^2, so the five codim-9 values of t are not related by the obvious symmetry.
K + x^2z^3 and K + x^3z^2 are not isomorphic, even over the algebraic closure: x <-> z exchanges the added terms but also reverses K, and the two curves have different Newton polygons.

At p=11, K alone has polygon 1/2^12 (codimension 12) in the old run4 and consistent runs2/run3. A real run2 curve record has the all-ones K vector, nonzero at zero-based coefficient positions 4, 6, and 19 (y^4z, xz^4, x^4y).
At p=11, K plus one monomial reaches 0^3 1/3^3 2/3^3 1^3 (codimension 3): run2 program 104 uses K+t*x^5, while run3 programs 206, 228, and 229 use K+t*z^5; each program has best score S=2.5.
explanation: Supersingularity of K: K is the Hurwitz curve H_{4,1}, which is supersingular exactly when some power of p is -1 mod 13 (Dawson et al., Thm 4.3); 7^6 = -1 mod 13. Equivalently, it is a quotient of the degree-13 Fermat curve (Shioda-Katsura).

Symmetry does not explain the deformations: the coordinate symmetries of K do not survive the added monomial (see observations), unlike the cyclic covers of entry 1, whose polygons are forced by the mu_5 symmetry they keep.

The deformations: unexplained. No published source treats K + t*m. Kloosterman's deformed-Fermat framework does not apply to either of the two orbits that differ. The slope pattern 1/3^6 2/3^6 in genus 6 does occur for degree-13 cyclic covers of P^1 branched at 3 points, with data (1,2,10), when p = 3 or 9 mod 13 (Li-Mantovan-Pries-Tang, Thm 5.4), but not at p = 7 and with no known link to this family.

Modulo 13 the successive powers of 11 are 11, 4, 5, 3, 7, 12; hence 11^6 = 12 = -1 and 11^12 = 1. None of the proper-divisor powers 11^1, 11^2, 11^3, 11^4, 11^6 is 1, so 11 has order 12 modulo 13. Dawson et al., Theorem 4.3, therefore predicts that K is supersingular at p=11.
open_questions: Why does the orbit of x^3z^2 reach codim 9 when the orbit of x^2z^3 reaches only codim 5?
Why is K - x^3z^2 supersingular? Is there a structure (an extra automorphism, a cover, a Fermat quotient) at t = -1?
Do the polygons stay constant in t over extensions of F_7, i.e. is 1/3^6 2/3^6 the generic polygon of the pencil over the algebraic closure?
What happens at other primes, e.g. by the residue of p mod 13?
references: E. Dawson, H. Frauenhoff, M. Lynch, A. Price, S. Somerstep, E. Work, D. Bisogno and R. Pries, The supersingularity of Hurwitz curves, Involve 12 (2019), 1293-1306. doi:10.2140/involve.2019.12.1293
P. Tzermias, Low-degree points on Hurwitz-Klein curves, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 356 (2004), 939-951. doi:10.1090/S0002-9947-03-03454-8

W. Li, E. Mantovan, R. Pries and Y. Tang, Newton polygons of cyclic covers of the projective line branched at three points, in Research Directions in Number Theory (WIN IV), AWM Series 19, Springer (2019), 115-132. arXiv:1805.04598
T. Shioda and T. Katsura, On Fermat varieties, Tohoku Math. J. 31 (1979), 97-115.

title: A mu_4-cover family at p=11
summary: Plane quintics F_5(x,z) + y^4 L_1(x,z) found at p=11 have Newton polygon 0^2 1/4^4 3/4^4 1^2 (codimension 4). Whether this is generic for the family at primes p congruent to 3 mod 4 remains open.

metadata.family: F_5(x,z) + y^4 L_1(x,z), with y occurring only through y^4

provenance.note: The consistent run has 57 OK samples with this polygon. A recorded curve is x^5 + x^3z^2 + xy^4 + y^4z + z^5.
The consistent run has 30 OK samples with this polygon; one recorded curve is x^5 + xz^4 + y^4z + 2z^5.
The old evaluator has 76 OK samples with this polygon. Its best recorded curve is x^5 + xz^4 + y^4z.

data: bead ne-scqh (old-evaluator p=11 run 4, first observation)
caveats: All polygons were computed with DeRham.jl 59b331b at table precision and are pending recomputation after the precision-bounds fix (bead ne-ez0l).
description: The family consists of smooth plane quintics C: F_5(x,z) + y^4 L_1(x,z) = 0, where F_5 is binary quintic and L_1 is linear. The variable y occurs only in y^4 terms.
observations: At p=11, the consistent run2 contains 57 OK samples and run3 contains 30 OK samples with polygon 0^2 1/4^4 3/4^4 1^2 (codimension 4); the old evaluator run4 contains 76 OK samples.
Run2 program 125 records x^5 + x^3z^2 + xy^4 + y^4z + z^5. Run4 records x^5 + xz^4 + y^4z as its best curve. In both examples, y occurs only as y^4.
explanation: Expectation only, not verified: y -> i*y gives a mu_4 action with quotient P^1. Since 11 = 3 mod 4 is inert in Q(i), this should force non-ordinary reduction, by analogy with the mu_5 argument in entry 1.
open_questions: Is codimension 4 the generic Newton polygon of this family at primes p congruent to 3 mod 4?
